symptom: The research-only shadow mapper normalized RFC 3339 -00:00 (unknown local UTC offset) through Date.parse and toISOString, silently converting unproven source timestamps into canonical UTC decision, odds, program-import and close instants. Node 22.16.0 parses -00:00 and +00:00 to the same instant; the downstream ledger validator cannot recover the lost offset provenance. Synthetic source-only fixture; no private evidence or production impact observed.
lesson: Known-offset validation must occur before source timestamp canonicalization: converting -00:00 to Z destroys the very uncertainty that a downstream exact-instant validator would otherwise reject. A normalized timestamp is not evidence that the source asserted a known UTC offset.
guardrail: Reject source timestamps ending in -00:00 before Date.parse/ISO conversion, including decision createdAt, odds fetchedAt, program importedAt and absolute scheduled closeAt. Retain explicit +00:00 and Z paths; assert unresolved reason codes for all four synthetic fields. This is provenance preservation, not external timestamp attestation or production authority.
